comparison: Both address C42 (competition assay). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED as a standard competitive binding demonstration. Peer review rates it UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 raising significant concerns about non-competitive effects at a different site, noting that PIP2 does not easily unbind.

Both address C63-C70, C110 (mutagenesis data on PIP2 binding site). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with systematic graded effects. Peer review rates it UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 concerned that mutations affecting PIP2 activation also influence Na-dependent inactivation independently of PIP2, making mechanistic interpretation ambiguous.

Both address C43-C46 (low-resolution cryo-EM with long-chain PIP2). Both rate as SUPPORTED/UNCERTAIN with similar reasoning: OpenEval notes low resolution (~11.5 Å) limits structural interpretation and C45 is explicitly speculative. Peer review accepts the technical limitation and rationale for using short-chain analog.

Both address C96-C101 (nonspecific electrostatic interactions with anionic lipids). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C96 is speculative but reasonable, well-supported by mutagenesis and literature. Peer review accepts the interpretation, though notes concern about untangling effects from Na-inactivation.

Both address C102-C105 (docking and native lipid density). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting computational predictions require experimental validation and lipid assignment is uncertain. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, accepting the docking analysis and native lipid observations without challenge.

Both address C71-C76 (SEA0400 structure determination). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes high resolution (2.9 Å) and detailed binding pocket observations. Peer review accepts the structural work, with Reviewer 2 noting it confirms previously reported structure.

Both address conformational changes from PIP2 diC8 binding (C52-C62 for OpenEval, C53, C57-C62 for peer). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes detailed structural observations with partial vs. complete destabilization. Peer review accepts conformational changes as 'mechanistically informative' and 'convincing insights.'

OpenEval R1 addresses C35-C37, C106-C107 (long-chain PIP2 electrophysiology). Peer R4 addresses C35-C41, C106-C109 (both long and short-chain PIP2 electrophysiology). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer review accepts the differential effects as high quality data central to the study's rationale.

OpenEval R2 addresses C38-C41, C108-C109 (short-chain PIP2 electrophysiology). Peer R4 addresses C35-C41, C106-C109 (both long and short-chain PIP2). Both rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the quantitative measurements distinguishing short-chain from long-chain effects.

OpenEval R4 addresses C47-C51 (PIP2 diC8 structure determination). Peer R1 addresses C5-C6, C47-C48, C71-C72 (overview of structural work). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer review explicitly affirms structural work as 'convincing insights' with 'high quality' data.

OpenEval R4 addresses C47-C51 (PIP2 diC8 structure). Peer R2 addresses C49-C56 (binding site details and conformational changes). Both rate as SUPPORTED, accepting structural observations without challenge.

OpenEval R5 addresses C52-C62 (detailed conformational changes). Peer R2 addresses C49-C56 (binding site and some conformational changes). Both rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the structural observations as high quality.

OpenEval R20 addresses C5-C7 (summary of structural contributions). Peer R1 addresses C5-C6, C47-C48, C71-C72 (overview of structural work). Both rate as SUPPORTED, affirming the primary structural achievements.

OpenEval R7 addresses C71-C76 (SEA0400 structure). Peer R1 addresses C5-C6, C47-C48, C71-C72 (overview of structural work including SEA0400). Both rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the structural determination.

Both address mechanistic explanation of SEA0400 inhibition (C79-C81 for OpenEval, C80-C81, C84, C92 for peer). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes steric clash inference is reasonable. Peer review accepts the mechanistic interpretation as 'convincing insights.'

OpenEval R10 addresses C82-C85 (reciprocal stabilization model). Peer R8 addresses C80-C81, C84, C92 (SEA0400 mechanism). Both rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic explanation connecting SEA0400 efficacy to inactivation state.

Both address C86-C88 (XIP removal and cytosolic accessibility). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with sound logic integrating prior work. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, noting 'interesting speculation' but lacking further experiments, requesting clarity on what extends beyond previous observations.

OpenEval R10 addresses C82-C85 (reciprocal stabilization). Peer R9 addresses C85-C88, C93-C95 (broader mechanistic claims). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculation without additional experiments.

OpenEval R15 addresses C89-C95 (integrated mechanistic framework). Peer R9 addresses C85-C88, C93-C95 (subset of mechanistic claims). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as major conceptual advance. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculation requires further testing.

Both address C8-C10 (major mechanistic conclusions). OpenEval R21 rates SUPPORTED as well-supported by data. Peer R13 rates SUPPORTED, affirming overall mechanistic conclusions as 'convincing insights' with 'key insights into NCX regulation.'

Both address integrated mechanistic framework (C89-C95 for OpenEval, C8-C10, C89-C91 for peer). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as major conceptual advance. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, affirming the integration of PIP2 and SEA0400 mechanisms.
